title: Dropping Python 3.10 support in PyIceberg
summary: Orest Tokovenko proposed dropping Python 3.10 from PyIceberg. Python 3.10 reached end of life on 2026-10-01, and pyarrow, a major dependency, no longer ships 3.10 wheels with its 26.x releases, so users on 3.10 get pyarrow 25.x while users on 3.11 and later get 26.x. He would set requires-python to >=3.11, raise the floor versions of some libraries (which would also allow moving the pyarrow floor from >=18.0.0 to >=26.0.0), and remove version gates in pyiceberg/io/pyarrow.py, all in one PR. Users on 3.10 can stay on the last release that supports it, as was done for 3.9 and 3.8. Fokko Driesprong agreed that end-of-life versions should not be supported and asked for a PR, which Tokovenko opened as iceberg-python #4170. Kevin Liu confirmed that the end-of-life date had just passed and thanked him.

positions.stance: PyIceberg should drop Python 3.10, require Python 3.11 or later, raise dependency floors and remove the version gates that are no longer needed.
End-of-life Python versions should not be supported, in line with how older versions were dropped before.

outcome.note: Both repliers agreed with dropping Python 3.10, and a PR (iceberg-python #4170) was opened; nobody objected.

why_it_matters: Once the PR merges, PyIceberg users on Python 3.10 have to stay on the last release that supports it.
